passage:
Room 804 started a class library with books brought by students. Anyone could borrow a book for one week. The only rule was to write a short comment before returning it.
At first, comments were simple: "Good," "Funny," or "Too long." Later, students wrote more carefully. They recommended books to friends and warned others about sad endings.
The comments helped students choose what to read next. Books that looked boring became popular after someone wrote an interesting comment.
The class library was small, but it felt personal. Each book carried not only the author's words, but also classmates' voices.
Reading became less lonely when students could leave thoughts for the next reader.
